literal: "They exist" that is said measure-they-are except, yielding-not barren land like-they-are learn-not-they.
translation: The unlearned are exactly like barren land that yields nothing, except for the mere fact that they can be said to exist.
modern: கல்லாதவர்கள் 'உயிரோடு இருக்கிறார்கள்' என்று சொல்லப்படும் அளவினரே தவிர, வேறு எந்தப் பயனும் தராத களர் நிலத்தைப் போன்றவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares uneducated people to barren, saline soil (களர்). Just as barren land occupies space but produces no crops, the unlearned occupy space in the world but produce nothing of value to themselves or others. The phrase 'உளர் என்னும் மாத்திரையர்' emphasizes that their only defining trait is their mere physical existence, while 'பயவா' (non-yielding) directly links the uselessness of the uncultivated land to the uncultivated mind.
